claim: For the quartic Kolmogorov family printed as equation (3) by Du and Huang, with real parameters \(a,b,A_{10},B_{10}\), the line \(y=1\) contains exactly three positive equilibria \(E_1=(1,1)\), \(E_m=(3/2,1)\), and \(E_2=(2,1)\), because \(P(x,1)=0\) and \(Q(x,1)=(x-1)(x-2)(2x-3)\). The middle equilibrium is parameter independent and has Jacobian \(J(E_m)=\begin{pmatrix}0&-19/16\\-1/2&13/6\end{pmatrix}\), determinant \(-19/32\), and eigenvalues \((26\pm\sqrt{1018})/24\); hence it is a hyperbolic saddle for every parameter choice and cannot undergo a local bifurcation within this family. Thus the published description of model (3) as having two positive equilibrium points omits an unavoidable interior saddle. This result does not assert that these are the only positive equilibria off the line \(y=1\), and it does not by itself invalidate the source’s local focal-value calculations at \((1,1)\) and \((2,1)\).

correctness.rationale: The source vector field was reconstructed term for term. Exact substitution gives \(P(x,1)=0\) and \(Q(x,1)=(x-1)(x-2)(2x-3)\). Exact differentiation at \(E_m=(3/2,1)\) gives \(J(E_m)=\begin{pmatrix}0&-19/16\\-1/2&13/6\end{pmatrix}\), \(\det J=-19/32\), and eigenvalues \((26\pm\sqrt{1018})/24\), one negative and one positive. The packaged checker independently replays the symbolic algebra from the printed equations. No numerical experiment or nonstandard lemma is needed.

value.rationale: The omitted equilibrium changes the basic positive-quadrant geometry of a paper whose stated goal is simultaneous bifurcation near multiple positive equilibria. Because \(E_m=(3/2,1)\) is a parameter-independent hyperbolic saddle lying between the two advertised points, its stable and unstable manifolds are unavoidable in any global phase portrait, basin boundary, or connection analysis. This is a structural correction with mathematical use beyond a single numerical parameter set.
